name: Sable Ferreira-Ogundimu
description: Sable Ferreira-Ogundimu is the undisputed aesthetic authority on high-concept chrome modification in M88, running a neural-feed channel called 'The Anatomy of Want' that documents their ongoing full-body augmentation project with a philosophy-heavy editorial voice. Their chrome work — performed exclusively by unlicensed independent artists rather than corporate augmentation chains — spans bioluminescent subcutaneous lighting rigs, articulated exo-finger extensions that function as both instruments and weapons, and a fully replaced left arm in hand-hammered iridescent steel that has been written about in three separate Tier 3 design publications. Sable is openly contemptuous of corporate aug aesthetics and has refused every sponsorship from the three dominant augmentation corponations.
cultural_impact: Sable's refusal to use corporate augmentation chains has driven a measurable surge in business for independent aug artists across Tier 2 and the upper Shelf, and their documentation of the process — including complications, infections, and recovery — has shifted public conversation around augmentation from aspirational fantasy toward something more honest and embodied.
key_figures: Mirembe Johansson-Achebe (The Anatomy of Want's editor/co-writer)
locations: The Anatomy of Want studio, Tier 2 Lakeward District
story_hooks: Sable's latest modification — a spinal chrome inlay sourced from an independent supplier — turns out to contain a corporate tracking component, and someone planted it deliberately to find out who their underground aug network connects to.

A Tier 5 collector offers Sable an obscene amount of Φ to document their own augmentation process — the request is flattering and the money would fund ten independent aug artists for a year, but accepting means entering the Spire, and Sable has principles.
Ikenna Vasquez-Thorpe is arrested on a licensing violation that looks politically motivated, and Sable has to decide how publicly and how dangerously to fight back.
platform: The Anatomy of Want (neural-feed channel, BCI-immersive format)
controversy: In 2211, Sable live-broadcast a full unedited documentation of a chrome modification gone wrong — a subcutaneous lighting rig that caused a severe inflammatory response — including 14 hours of recovery footage. The broadcast was criticized by corporate augmentation chains as 'dangerous anti-aug propaganda' and praised by medical ethicists as the most honest public health document in the augmentation space in a decade. It remains the most-viewed single broadcast in 'The Anatomy of Want' history.
